title: Read-only sed checker skips the rest of a script after an unknown character at command start; `w`/`e` writes pass on master
outcome: claude_sed_script_can_write (src/claude.rs, about :1443 on master 9ce9b521) parses sed scripts fail-closed. Addresses are recognized (N, $, /re/, \cREc with any delimiter, first~step, addr,+N and addr,~N, the I and M flags, !). After them, only a known command letter is accepted; w, W, e and any write-capable or unknown construct are refused. A read-only reviewer can no longer write files through sed on any read-only path (Claude adapter, strict, Kimi, engram_command_reads_only). Regression tests cover each bypass spelling on every path.
acceptance:
C1 (script parser, fail closed). claude_sed_script_can_write parses each sed script command by command and treats the script as read-only only when every command is understood.
- Addresses: a line number, first~step, $, /re/ and \cREc with any delimiter c, each regex optionally followed by I or M; a second address of any of these or +N or ~N; then optional '!'.
- Commands accepted: { } = d D g G h H l [N] n N p P q [N] Q [N] x z F, : b t T with a label of [A-Za-z0-9_.-], a/i/c with their text, # comments, s and y with their sections, and s flags g p I i M m and digits.
- Commands refused: w W e r R; s flags w W e; any other command letter.
- Also refused: an unterminated address, regex, s or y; a bracket expression in a regex that contains the delimiter, or one left unclosed; a \c escape in an s or y section, or in an address regex; and any character after a command other than whitespace, ';', '}' or '#'.

C3 (tests, on every read-only path that checks sed on master: the Claude permission adapter, the strict checker, Kimi's gate and engram_command_reads_only).

REFUSED:
- `sed -n '\%foo%w victim.txt' input.txt`
- `sed -n '1~2w out' f`
- `sed -n '$!w out' f`
- `sed -n '/x/!w out' f`
- `sed -n '/x/Iw out' f`
- `sed -n '/x/Mw out' f`
- `sed -n '0,/x/w out' f`
- `sed -n '1,+2w out' f`
- `sed -n '1,~4w out' f`
- `sed -n '/x/{w out' f`
- `sed '1e touch x' f`
- `sed 's/a/b/e' f`
- `sed 's/a/b/w out' f`
- `sed -n '\%x%e touch y' f`
- `sed -n --expression='1w out' f`
- `sed -n --expression '1w out' f`
- `sed -ni 's/a/b/' f`
- `sed -si 's/a/b/' f`
- `sed --in-pl 's/a/b/' f`
- `sed -n 's/[/]/x/w out' f`
- `sed 'r /etc/passwd' f`
- `sed -n 'p w' f`

ACCEPTED:
- `sed -n '1,10p' f`
- `sed 's/a/b/' f`
- `sed 's#a#b#g' f`
- `sed -n '/^[a-z]/p' f`
- `sed -n '/[[:alpha:]]/p' f`
- `sed -n '$p' f`
- `sed -n '2~3p' f`
- `sed -n '/x/,/y/p' f`
- `sed '/x/d' f`
- `sed -ne '1p' f`
- `sed --quiet -e '1,3p' f`
- `sed -n '/x/!p' f`

Every existing read-only checker test still passes unchanged.

C4 (validation and landing). The full gate passes on the exact tree submitted for landing; the review pair has no outstanding finding of Medium or higher on it; and the item carries the evidence the standing landing rule requires.
